\section[el terapeuta]{el terapeuta — the therapist}

\label{lesson:ES-C743-terapeuta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for exercise, then the Spanish for to chew.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el terapeuta}
\textbf{el terapeuta} — \textquotedblleft{}the therapist\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mi terapeuta me escucha mucho.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My therapist really listens to me.}
\end{quote}

Same form for men and women.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{terapeuta} comes from Greek \emph{therapeut\'{\={e}}s} \textquotedblleft{}attendant\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{therapeúein} \textquotedblleft{}to serve, to treat\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el terapeuta}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el terapeuta}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el terapeuta}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for exercise, then the Spanish for to chew, then say \emph{el terapeuta} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el terapeuta mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The therapist\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la terapia]{la terapia — therapy}

\label{lesson:ES-C743-terapia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to chew, then the Spanish for the therapist.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la terapia}
\textbf{la terapia} — \textquotedblleft{}therapy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Voy a terapia una vez por semana.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I go to therapy once a week.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{terapia} comes from Greek \emph{therapeía} \textquotedblleft{}service, medical treatment\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{therapeúein} \textquotedblleft{}to serve, to treat\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[el psicólogo]{el psicólogo — the psychologist}

\label{lesson:ES-C743-psicologo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the therapist, then the Spanish for therapy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el psicólogo}
\textbf{el psicólogo} — \textquotedblleft{}the psychologist\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mi hermana es psicóloga.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My sister is a psychologist.}
\end{quote}

The \emph{p} is often silent in speech; \emph{sicólogo} is also accepted.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{psicólogo} is built on Greek \emph{psykh\'{\={e}}} \textquotedblleft{}breath, soul, mind\textquotedblright{} and \emph{lógos} \textquotedblleft{}word, study\textquotedblright{}: one who studies the mind.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el psicólogo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el psicólogo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el psicólogo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the therapist, then the Spanish for therapy, then say \emph{el psicólogo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el psicólogo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The psychologist\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el bienestar]{el bienestar — well-being}

\label{lesson:ES-C743-bienestar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for therapy, then the Spanish for the psychologist.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el bienestar}
\textbf{el bienestar} — \textquotedblleft{}well-being\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El deporte mejora el bienestar.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bienestar} is built on \emph{bien} \textquotedblleft{}well\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{bene}, and \emph{estar} \textquotedblleft{}to be\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{stāre} \textquotedblleft{}to stand\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la autoestima]{la autoestima — self-esteem}

\label{lesson:ES-C743-autoestima}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the psychologist, then the Spanish for well-being.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la autoestima}
\textbf{la autoestima} — \textquotedblleft{}self-esteem\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tiene la autoestima muy baja.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He has very low self-esteem.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{autoestima} is built on Greek \emph{autós} \textquotedblleft{}self\textquotedblright{} and \emph{estima} \textquotedblleft{}esteem\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{estimar}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{aestimāre} \textquotedblleft{}to value\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the psychologist, then the Spanish for well-being, then say \emph{la autoestima} again

\section[(dialogue)]{Repaso de los capítulos 736–743}

\label{lesson:ES-R743-repaso-736-743}



\begin{quote}
Say the Spanish for the forehead and the cheek.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the forehead, the cheek, the chin, the beard, the ear
  \item the elbow, the wrist, the waist, the hip, the rib
  \item the diagnosis, to diagnose, the symptom, the treatment, to suffer from
  \item to cure, to get better, recovery, to operate, surgery
  \item nausea, to relieve, to vomit, to faint, the allergy
  \item tiredness, exhausted, to fall asleep, insomnia, the nap
  \item the diet, excess weight, appetite, exercise, to chew
  \item the therapist, therapy, the psychologist, well-being, self-esteem
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The forehead? (\textbf{la frente}.) The cheek? (\textbf{la mejilla}.) The chin? (\textbf{la barbilla}.) The beard? (\textbf{la barba}.) The ear? (\textbf{la oreja}.) The elbow? (\textbf{el codo}.) The wrist? (\textbf{la muñeca}.) The waist? (\textbf{la cintura}.) The hip? (\textbf{la cadera}.) The rib? (\textbf{la costilla}.) The diagnosis? (\textbf{el diagnóstico}.) To diagnose? (\textbf{diagnosticar}.) The symptom? (\textbf{el síntoma}.) The treatment? (\textbf{el tratamiento}.) To suffer from? (\textbf{padecer}.) To cure? (\textbf{curar}.) To get better? (\textbf{mejorarse}.) Recovery? (\textbf{la recuperación}.) To operate? (\textbf{operar}.) Surgery? (\textbf{la cirugía}.) Nausea? (\textbf{las náuseas}.) To relieve? (\textbf{aliviar}.) To vomit? (\textbf{vomitar}.) To faint? (\textbf{desmayarse}.) The allergy? (\textbf{la alergia}.) Tiredness? (\textbf{el cansancio}.) Exhausted? (\textbf{agotado}.) To fall asleep? (\textbf{dormirse}.) Insomnia? (\textbf{el insomnio}.) The nap? (\textbf{la siesta}.) The diet? (\textbf{la dieta}.) Excess weight? (\textbf{el sobrepeso}.) Appetite? (\textbf{el apetito}.) Exercise? (\textbf{el ejercicio}.) To chew? (\textbf{masticar}.) The therapist? (\textbf{el terapeuta}.) Therapy? (\textbf{la terapia}.) The psychologist? (\textbf{el psicólogo}.) Well-being? (\textbf{el bienestar}.) Self-esteem? (\textbf{la autoestima}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
